er.comment: Detection.md entry 10: `erDiagram`, exact. The lexer then reads the header again, case-insensitively and not followed by a word character. er.md#detection: The lexer then reads the header again, case-insensitively and not followed by a word character (see [The statement context](#the-statement-context)). So `erDiagramX` is detected as an ER diagram and rejected, while `erDiagram-x` is the header followed by the entity `-x`. patterns.comment: A line or paragraph separator leading through whitespace and directives to a common comment is trivia rather than the non-ASCII part of an ER name. er.md#entities: - The alias is an entity name between `[` and `]`, with whitespace around it or not: `p[Person]`, `p [ Person ]`, `p["Per son"]`, `p[12]`, `p[1]`, `"A"[P]`, `12[P]`, and `1[P]` are entities with an alias. `p[]` and `p[A B]` are rejected. The alias comes before the classes, and an entity with an alias takes no relationship on its line: `A:::c[P]`, `p[P] ||--o{ B : x`, `p[P]:::c ||--o{ B : x`, `A ||--o{ p[P] : x`, and `A:::c ||--o{ p[P] : x` are rejected, while `p[P]:::c`, `p[P] { … }`, `p[P]:::c { … }`, and `p[P]:::c {}` are accepted. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Rules 19 to 21: bounded class, subgraph and end are keywords, compared case-insensitively. er.md#the-statement-context: **The cardinalities, numbers, and relationship lines.** Rule 22 tries these rules in order; each makes one unit named after the cardinality or the line, whatever its spelling: `zero-or-one`, `zero-or-more`, `one-or-more`, `only-one`, and `md-parent` for a cardinality, `identifying` and `non-identifying` for a relationship line, and `number` for a number. An entity placeholder is part of a name. er.md#units-and-contexts: **Names.** In the statement context, one or more characters each of which is a character outside ASCII, a word character, `-`, `*`, or `.`, as many as possible, make a `name` unit: `ÀB-c.d*e`, `_a`, an emoji, and `C4Context` are names, while `#`, `,`, `;`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `|`, `:`, `=`, `+`, `/`, `&`, `@`, `$`, `!`, `^`, `` ` ``, `~`, and `?` are not characters of a name; a line that holds a name and one of them is rejected, as the `?` of `Blo?rf` is, unless the character starts a unit of its own.

er-direction.comment: TB, BT, RL and LR are tried in this order, at the last direction for that value; surrounding runs are direction-text. Directives inside those runs join their parts and cannot supply direction or its value; directives between components are trivia. Runs stop before separator-led common comments, and padding never consumes their separator. er.md#the-statement-context: **The direction line.** Compared case-insensitively: from the current position, a run of characters without line feeds, U+2028, or U+2029, the longest one that the rest can follow; then `direction`; then one or more whitespace characters, line feeds included; then one of `TB`, `BT`, `RL`, and `LR`, tried in this order; and then every character up to the next line feed. The rule reads `direction` as a `direction` unit, the value as a `direction-value` unit, and the characters before `direction` and after the value as `direction-text` units, which mermaid.js does not read. The rule is tried before the whitespace and name rules, so it takes the whole line: `A direction LR` sets the direction and has no entity, and so do `A ||--o{ B : x direction LR` and `A ||--o{ B : direction TB`; `Direction lr` and `DIRECTION tb` are direction lines, and the indentation before `direction` is part of the run. It is also tried before the keyword rules that follow it: `classDef a direction LR` sets the direction and defines no class, `A accTitle: direction LR` sets the direction, and `subgraph direction LR` is a direction line, so that the `end` after it closes nothing and is rejected; only rules 1 to 3 come before it, so `accTitle: direction LR` is a title. Neither does the value need to end at a word boundary: `direction LRX` sets `LR`, and `X` is a `direction-text` unit; `direction LR %% c` sets `LR` with the text `%% c`, and `direction LR;` with the text `;`. The values are tried in the order given: if the line has `direction`, whitespace, and `TB` anywhere, the value is `TB`; otherwise `BT` is tried, and so on. For a value, the lexer takes the last `direction` of the run that the value follows. So `direction TB x direction TB` is read at its last `direction`, and `direction TB x` is a `direction-text` unit, while `direction TB x direction LR` and `direction TBx direction RL` set `TB` and are read at their first `direction`, with the rest as a `direction-text` unit. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
